claim: Rocca Roveresca opens daily 8:30 a.m.-7:30 p.m. (ticket office closes 7:00 p.m.), closed Dec 25 and Jan 1; full ticket EUR5, reduced EUR2 (ages 18-25), under-18 free.
quote: From Monday to Sunday 8.30 a.m. - 7.30 p.m. ... Standard ticket: EUR5.00 ... Reduced (ages 18-25): EUR2.00 ... closed on December 25th and January 1st.

claim: The Rocca Roveresca was rebuilt into a Renaissance fortress under Giovanni della Rovere in the late 15th century by architects Luciano Laurana and Baccio Pontelli, also serving as a noble palace and seat of an artillery academy founded by Guidubaldo della Rovere in 1533.
quote: Giovanni della Rovere commissioning renowned architects Luciano Laurana and Baccio Pontelli to reconstruct the fortress into a Renaissance masterpiece ... seat of an artillery academy founded by Guidubaldo della Rovere in 1533.

claim: The Foro Annonario, a circular neoclassical brick market designed by Senigallia architect Pietro Ghinelli in 1834, has a portico of 24 Doric columns, hosts a daily fruit-and-vegetable market with food and wine shops, and now also holds the Antonelliana Library and Municipal Archives.
quote: Pietro Ghinelli designed this neoclassical structure in 1834 ... a complex of 24 columns with Doric-style capitals ... houses a daily fruit and vegetable market ... now hosts the Antonelliana Library and Municipal Archives.

claim: The Foro Annonario was conceived as an urban backdrop for the river axis parallel to the eighteenth-century Portici Ercolani, with its construction spanning roughly 1810 to 1847.
quote: the idea of creating a new square as an urban backdrop for the river axis, parallel to the eighteenth-century Portici Ercolani

claim: The Portici Ercolani run along the right bank of the Misa river as 126 Istrian-stone arches, designed by Monsignor Giuseppe Ercolani in the mid-18th century on the order of Pope Benedict XIV as the venue for the Fiera Franca trade fair, replacing the old fortress walls.
quote: 126 magnificent Istrian-stone arcades ... named after Monsignor Giuseppe Ercolani (1677-1759), who designed them in the mid of the 18th century upon order of Pope Benedict XIV ... as the celebration venue for the famous Fiera Franca (Trade Fair).

claim: The Portici Ercolani still host trade, filling with stalls for the St. Augustine fair (Aug 28-30) and every Thursday for the weekly open-air market; a scenic walk runs from the Vecchia Filanda in Piazza Garibaldi toward the Rione Porto harbour district.
quote: every Thursday of the year for the weekly open air market ... A suggested walk under the silent arcades of Portici Ercolani starts from Vecchia Filanda (Old Spinning Mill) in Piazza Garibaldi towards Rione Porto

claim: Palazzetto Baviera, overlooking Piazza del Duca, was built for Giovanni Giacomo Baviera (Giovanni della Rovere's uncle) and its main floor holds ceilings entirely decorated in stucco by Federico Brandani of Urbino across five themed rooms (Imperial Rome, Republican Rome, the Iliad, Hercules, the Old Testament).
quote: ceilings entirely decorated in stucco by Federico Brandani from Urbino ... The ceilings of the five rooms (of Imperial Rome, Republican Rome, the Iliad, Hercules, the Old Testament) are undoubtedly the greatest expression of Federico Brandani's work.

claim: Piazza del Duca, named for Giovanni della Rovere and once used for parades and military exercises, holds the 1596 Fontana delle Anatre (also called fonte del Duca or dei Leoni) in pink marble with bronze decorations, set off-center because of the parade ground.
quote: la beautiful Fontana delle Anatre ... del 1596 in pink marble with bronze decorations ... used as a place for parades and military exercises ... the Fontana delle Anatre (or dei Leoni) is off-center with respect to the plan.

claim: Senigallia's Duomo, the Cathedral of San Pietro Apostolo, was built 1762-1790 to a design by Paolo Posi on a former Jesuit church, with a neoclassical two-order facade (Doric below, Ionic above) remade in 1877 by Augusto Innocenti and financed by Senigallia-born Pope Pius IX.
quote: built according to the project of architect Paolo Posi ... between 1762 and 1790 ... The facade, in neoclassical style with two superimposed orders (Doric in the lower part, Ionic in the upper), was remade in 1877, based on a design by Augusto Innocenti ... financed by Pope Pio IX, who originated from Senigallia.
